! at a non-top-level unary position compiles to unary_bang; NOT/top-level ! compile to the not opcode instead (see legacy.json for the bare and/or opcodes and short_circuit.json for the jump opcodes)

the undefined literal (px-ocp): a source spelling for a lit operand the ISA's value domain already admitted (docs/isa.md section 3), so no ISA version moves - surface syntax is outside the ISA (section 6)
the non-strict operators propagate :undefined rather than answering (docs/reference/language.md, reject vs. propagate) - === is the boundness test, == is not

px-o9v: null and undefined are distinct values - === answers false rather than treating a bound null the same as an absent binding. There is no null literal in the grammar, so the null comes from context rather than a source spelling
px-o9v: null === null mirrors undefined === undefined
px-o9v: == is a typed comparison and null has no type peer, so every non-strict comparison involving null propagates :undefined rather than answering - by exact symmetry with undefined == undefined
px-o9v: null == null is :undefined, not true - null has no ordering and no == peer, unlike null === null (core/null-strict-eq-null)
px-o9v: null is falsy at a jump, joining false and :undefined - x short-circuits the AND and its own value (null) is the result, true is never evaluated

px-o9v: null is falsy at a jump but not is not a jump - not, unary_bang, unary_minus, and the arithmetic opcodes all reject null with a TypeMismatchError, the same as every non-boolean, non-jump operand
